details.label: Discussion
details.text: In the presence of steep low/mid-level lapse rates and weak background forcing for ascent, thunderstorms are gradually increasing over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and adjacent Raton Mesa. Latest HRRR and RRFS time-lagged ensemble guidance indicates a subsequent eastward movement of the developing storms toward the OK and TX Panhandle between 21Z-23Z. While overall CAPE will remain somewhat marginal (750-1000 J/kg), the presence of lapse rates greater than 8-8.5 C/km and effective bulk shear of around 25 kt will support some organization of the high-based storms, which are rooted atop a hot, well-mixed boundary layer. Latest CAM data remain in good agreement in depicting storm clustering by early to mid evening along a strengthening cold pool. Initially isolated occurrences of severe winds may become more numerous at that time along with an increased potential for gusts up to 70-80 mph

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest water vapor imagery depicts a well-defined mid-level shortwave trough centered over southeastern Manitoba, with surface analysis indicating this low is vertical stacked with its surface reflection. To the southeast of this feature, an increase in cumulus development has been noted over the past 30-60 minutes across portions of northern Minnesota along a surface cold front. Ahead of this front, temperatures in the mid-to-upper 70s F and 60s F dewpoints are supporting 1000-1500+ J/kg MLCAPE, with latest objective analysis suggesting minimal MLCIN remains. As convective initiation occurs along the front, supercells will be possible initially. While mid-level lapse rates and effective shear will generally remain modest (around 6-6.5 C/km and 25-35 kts, respectively), large hail will be possible, especially farther north where cooler mid-level temperatures should allow for marginally steeper mid-level lapse rates. The expectation is then for multicells/clusters and an associated risk for damaging wind gusts to be increasingly favored with time as storm coverage increases through the afternoon along the eastward-progressing front. A brief tornado also cannot be ruled out given modestly enhanced low-level shear/hodograph curvature sampled by the Duluth VWP and indicated by recent mesoanalysis/RAP forecast soundings. A WW may be needed in the next 1-2 hours pending further convective development
